before: Returning &str borrowed from an input can be valid because the caller owns the underlying String. With one input reference, lifetime elision relates that input to the returned reference.

A String created inside a function is dropped when that function returns unless ownership leaves the function. Returning a slice into that local would dangle, so safe Rust rejects it. Adding a lifetime label cannot repair the owner’s early destruction; return an owned String instead when appropriate.
Expected output or behavior: alive. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

before.question: If view creates a local String and returns &local instead, what happens?
choices: The lifetime annotation keeps local alive automatically.
Compilation rejects returning a reference to the local owner.
The reference becomes an empty slice.
before.explanation: The local String would be destroyed before the caller could use its slice; returning ownership would be a different valid design.

after.question: Could the function return a borrow of a new String that belongs only to the function?
choices: Yes. Returning a borrow copies the text.
No. That String goes away when the function ends.
Yes. Every local String lives forever.
after.explanation: The local String would disappear before the caller could use the borrowed view.
